Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bioLeak 0.4.0

Dependency changes

  • SummarizedExperiment moved from Imports to Suggests, so install.packages("bioLeak") no longer fails when the Bioconductor package is not installed (JSS review, J10). It is needed only for SummarizedExperiment input; such input without it now stops with an install hint.

Bug fixes (results can change)

  • The batch confounding alarm tested the wrong table (JSS review, L1.1-L1.3). confounding_alignment was flagged from a fold x batch chi-square test, which ignores the outcome: it could not detect batch confounding and fired for blocked designs (V = 1 by construction). It now flags only when both conditions for batch-driven optimism hold: batch is associated with the outcome (new batch-outcome test in batch_assoc: chi-square with Cramer’s V for classification, Kruskal-Wallis with epsilon^2 for regression; run on the plan’s independent units, one observation per subject or group when the plan records one, including a subject constraint of a combined plan; time-series plans without a group and survival outcomes are not tested; Holm across batch columns, p <= 0.05 and at least a small effect) and batches are shared by training and test rows (new span_frac > 0). Blocked designs have span_frac = 0 and are never flagged. The fold x batch test is still reported and described as a fold-batch test. When batch varies within subjects, association within subjects (e.g. paired tumour and normal samples in different batches) is not tested; its row-level effect size is reported (within_unit_effect) and printed by summary(). audit_leakage_by_learner() prints the batch-outcome evidence instead of the fold-batch table. In simulations (200 datasets per design) the null flag rate was 0.000-0.080 (limit 0.096) across 14 designs: one row per subject, repeated rows per subject, batch varying within subjects (equal, unequal, 1-2 samples per subject, time-ordered, pairs mixed with singletons), multiclass outcomes, rsample grouped folds, leave-study-out and combined plans with a subject column, and time series; blocked designs were never flagged; under a clear batch-outcome association with shared batches the flag rate was 0.98-1.00.

  • Plots were not drawn in knitted documents. The plot_*() functions printed only in interactive sessions, so the vignette and rendered reports showed none of their figures; they now also print while knitting.

  • summary(<LeakAudit>) reported “Repeats: 1” for repeated plans (it read the fit’s metadata instead of the plan’s).

  • delta_lsi() now warns when M_boot, M_flip or seed are supplied: they belonged to the former bootstrap / sign-flip inference and have no effect on the corrected t-test (they were silently ignored).

  • Imputation did nothing when a training fold had no missing values. The guard then recorded “no imputation” whatever method was requested, so missing values in the test rows stayed NA and those predictions were dropped silently (in leave-study-out CV, a study that never measured a feature disappeared from the results without a warning). The requested method is now always fitted; missForest has no per-column model then and falls back to the training medians with a warning.

  • Stratified fold assignment lost folds. Each class was dealt to folds starting from fold 1, so classes with fewer groups than v left high-numbered folds empty (6 of 10 requested folds) and fold sizes uneven. Units are now dealt round-robin across classes, so all folds are kept and get an almost equal number of groups, with each class spread as evenly as possible (per-fold class proportions can vary slightly more than before, the trade-off for equal fold sizes). Stratified plans can differ from earlier versions for the same seed.

  • positive_class set to the first level failed with recipes and workflows (“wrong attributes: y”): the outcome was releveled after the recipe captured its level order. Recipes and workflows now receive the original level order, and tune_resample() points tune’s event level at the positive class. Probability columns are now looked up by the exact level name (.pred_1, .pred_case 1) before its make.names() form, and a missing positive-class column is an error: falling back to “the second column” would have scored the negative class for non-syntactic level names (AUC 0.09 instead of 0.91 in a test).

  • Multiclass yardstick metric sets with class probabilities failed (“Failed to compute roc_auc()”) because the probability columns were passed as named arguments.

  • Audit p-values were too small with repeated CV, clustered samples or autocorrelated series. The fixed-prediction permutation gap (perm_refit = FALSE, or “auto” without a stored refit specification or with B > 200) shuffled pooled prediction rows independently: a sample’s copies from repeated CV got different labels, a subject’s correlated samples were treated as independent, and time order was ignored (type-I at alpha = 0.05: 0.16-0.23 with 5 repeats, 0.17-0.19 with clustered samples, 0.27 with AR(0.9) series). Labels are now permuted per sample (copies share one label); in subject-grouped plans (and combined plans, via their primary axis, and time-series plans with a group) whole subjects swap label vectors with subjects of the same size and labels are shuffled within subjects, which keeps the class balance exact and lets paired designs (one case and one control sample per subject) flip within pairs; a warning says when few subjects can be exchanged; in time-series plans without a group labels move in time blocks. Type-I: 0.058, 0.042, 0.083 (limit 0.11). The multivariate target scan, which refits on each permuted outcome, used a free shuffle in grouped, batch and study designs (0.31 with clustered samples); it now uses the same subject-level scheme or the refit audits’ restricted permutation (0.025). The refit null’s element-wise shuffle across subjects of unique size (0.147 in small uneven cohorts) is replaced by the same scheme. When every permutation gives the same value (e.g. subject size determines the outcome) a warning says the p-value is uninformative. perm_summary = "fold_mean" is not calibrated for fixed predictions (0.11-0.14) and now falls back to “pooled” with a warning.

  • Duplicate detection flagged ordinary tabular data. Rows were compared on uncentred columns, so unrelated patients looked near-identical (1803 of 11175 pairs without duplicates). Columns are now centred and pairs must also lie at a similar distance from the column means (0 false pairs with 6 tabular features; true copies are still found). Pairs must also be much closer than typical pairs (within 10% of the median distance), and with fewer than 5 features, where close pairs arise by chance, only identical rows are reported. Noisy technical replicates (e.g. low-depth re-sequencing) can fall below sim_threshold; lower it to look for them.

  • Leave-batch-out and leave-study-out plans were flagged as confounded. The batch association test flagged the column the split blocks on, which aligns with the folds by design. Rows for the axis the split mode blocks on (batch for batch_blocked, study for study_loocv, group, constraint axes), and columns nested within that axis (e.g. site within study), are now marked by_design and do not trigger confounding_alignment; a batch merely recorded on a subject-grouped plan is still tested.

  • The audit summary could overstate the result. Its interpretation used the gap size alone (“Strong non-random signal” at p = 0.15); it now prints and uses the permutation p-value, and notes that a significant gap does not rule out leakage. The report template said a non-significant gap “warns of leakage” (leakage makes the gap larger); corrected. “Batch / Study Association: none detected” is now “not tested” when no column was tested.

  • tune_resample() tuned on an inverted AUC. Its auc / roc_auc / pr_auc metrics set event_level = "second" on the metric, but tune passes the first class’s probability column, so inner AUCs were 1 minus their value (0.14 for a model with AUC 0.85) and the worst setting was chosen in every outer fold (the default metrics). The event level is now set through control$event_level, and the plain metrics are used.

  • tune_resample() input fixes. A numeric 0/1 outcome (accepted by fit_resample()) now works; it failed every inner fit with a misleading stratification hint (with a recipe or workflow, a non-factor class outcome gets a clear error). Plans from as_leaksplits() now work without nested = TRUE (inner folds are built from the spec’s design columns stored in the plan; before: “Column ‘group_id’ not found”). rsample input works: rsample plans record no seed, which reached set.seed() as NA, and rsample::nested_cv() inner resamples were never read. rsets without the bioLeak_mode attribute now use the design inferred at import (as in fit_resample()), and nested_cv() needs no inferable design column. When single-class inner folds force AUC out of tuning, the remaining metrics are kept (all were dropped and the call failed, e.g. with bootstraps()). Inner folds now also use the plan’s stratify_by.

  • Split columns could reach the model through a recipe. With preprocess = <recipe>, the recipe was prepped on data that still held the split columns (group, batch, study, time, stratify_by, sample id) and only exact column names were removed afterwards, so a standard recipe(y ~ .) |> step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) passed their dummy columns to the learner (CV AUC 1.0 on pure noise with an outcome-derived stratum). Those columns now get the non-predictor role "bioLeak_split" before prep(), in fit_resample(), tune_resample() and for workflows whose recipe lists them; steps may still name them, but neither they nor anything derived from them is a predictor. Steps that select by type (step_dummy(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes())) bypass roles; such recipes are now detected after prep() (predictors that change when the split columns are shifted) and stop with an error naming the derived columns.

  • tune_resample() used the group column as a predictor when given a parsnip model and no recipe (outcome ~ . on the full data), so held-out subjects were new factor levels and outer folds were silently skipped (6 of 15 in a test). Split columns are now removed, as in fit_resample(). A recipe defined on the full data (y ~ .), given as preprocess or in a workflow, also works in tune_resample() now; it failed with “Not all variables in the recipe are present”.

  • audit_leakage(perm_refit = TRUE) on as_leaksplits() plans ignored or broke the design. The refit permutation metadata came from the user’s data, which lacks the spec’s design columns (group_id, batch_group, study_group): batch and study specs failed (“Batch column not found for batch_blocked mode”), and subject specs fell back to an unrestricted label shuffle with a warning. Those columns are now joined from the plan by sample id (also into a user-supplied perm_refit_spec$coldata), giving the same restricted null as an equivalent make_split_plan() plan. When a design column is genuinely unavailable, batch, study and time designs now fall back to the documented unrestricted shuffle with a warning instead of erroring.

  • perm_stratify made batch and study refit nulls the identity. Refit permutations for batch_blocked / study_loocv permute labels within each batch or study; stratifying that by the outcome permuted within batch x outcome cells, so no label moved and p was 1. perm_stratify is now ignored there with a warning.

  • audit_leakage() re-drawn plans kept the sample id as a predictor. For plans from as_leaksplits(), perm_folds = "auto" re-drew the folds without the record that sample_id is an identifier, so every permutation refit encoded it as a predictor (with glm, all permutation values and the p-value were NA). The re-drawn plan now keeps it.

  • metric_summary intervals could belong to another learner. With several learners given in non-alphabetical order (e.g. c("ranger", "glmnet")), fit_resample() copied cv_ci()’s interval columns by position into a summary sorted by learner name, so each learner could be shown another learner’s interval. They are now matched by name.

  • Repeated rsample resamples had fold and repeat swapped. rsample’s repeated designs (vfold_cv(repeats = ), group_vfold_cv(repeats = )) put the repeat in id and the fold in id2; bioLeak read them the other way round, so delta_lsi() and cv_ci() used the wrong number of folds per repeat (e.g. 19 instead of 4 degrees of freedom for 5 folds x 20 repeats, too-small p-values and too-narrow intervals). as_rsample() dropped the repeat column for repeated plans (rsample’s manual_rset() has none), so a round trip also lost the repeats. Both directions now follow rsample’s convention; older exports with repeated "FoldK" ids are still read correctly. tibble is added to Suggests for the export.

  • splits@info$stratify now says whether stratification was applied. Rolling-origin time_series folds are never stratified; stratify = TRUE there now warns and is recorded as FALSE (only the grouped panel fallback stratifies). A missing stratify_by column is also recorded as unstratified. A given stratify_by column is always recorded, applied or not, so fit_resample() / tune_resample() keep it out of the predictors. as_leaksplits() no longer requests stratification for ordered specs. Previously the plan claimed a stratification it did not have, and audit_leakage(perm_folds = "auto") re-drew such plans needlessly.

  • Survival C-index was inverted. survival::concordance() treats higher predictions as longer survival, but bioLeak’s survival predictions are risk scores, so every survival C-index (fit metrics, audits, delta_lsi()) was reported as 1 minus its value; a strong risk model scored about 0.2. The C-index now treats predictions as risk scores (higher = shorter survival), the convention custom learners are documented to follow. Survival models given as parsnip specs or workflows, which previously failed to predict, now use linear_pred (else time). Engines do not agree on the direction of these outputs (censored’s rpart time rises with hazard, survreg’s with survival), so the direction is decided on each training fold and the predictions are turned into a risk score; test rows are not used. When the direction cannot be decided (e.g. no comparable pairs in an all-censored training fold), that fold’s predictions are NA and left out of the metrics, reported in one warning across folds.

  • cv_ci() counts repeated identical test sets once, as delta_lsi() does, and accepts a LeakTune; repeated leave-one-batch-out intervals were too narrow.

  • plot(<LeakDeltaLSI>) shows deltas on the inflation scale for lower-is-better metrics too (points were sign-flipped against the line and band), and returns the object’s R_eff.

  • Grouped time series keeps the better of the regular folds and the panel fallback (the plan that tests more rows), instead of e.g. a single fold training on 2 rows; tied times are named as a reason for dropped blocks.

  • nested = TRUE no longer fails the whole plan when an inner split cannot be built for some outer fold.

  • as_leaksplits(use_block_constraints = ) can enforce a chosen subset. spec$block_vars lists the blocking annotations available in a splitGraph spec, which can be many (batch, study, site, …). use_block_constraints now also takes a character vector naming the block_vars to enforce (TRUE still enforces all; unknown names are an error that lists the available ones). When excluding shared levels empties every fold’s training set, the error now names the axes and their level counts and suggests a smaller set, instead of “No valid folds generated”; when only some folds survive and rows are never tested, a warning reports the coverage. The option is ignored for non-grouped specs with a warning (previously silently), and overriding mode / constraints through ... warns that it no longer applies.

  • Batch adjustment no longer skips rows silently. guard_fit()’s steps$batch_adjust now applies a policy, unseen = c("warn", "error", "grand_mean"), to rows whose batch was not seen in training, rows with a missing batch label, and transform() calls without batch labels. All of these were left unadjusted with no message. Under batch-blocked or study-held-out CV every test batch is unseen; fit_resample() reports this once (“in k of K folds …”) instead of per fold. A single training batch now applies no adjustment with a warning instead of failing.

  • Batch adjustment warns when batch and outcome are confounded, and can protect the outcome. When batch is associated with y in the training data (p < 0.01), removing batch effects also removes part of the outcome signal, so performance is underestimated; this now warns. The new opt-in protect = TRUE estimates batch effects net of the outcome (z ~ batch + y, the role of ComBat’s mod), which keeps the signal but can bias cross-validated performance upward (Nygaard et al., 2016): about +0.03 to +0.10 AUC with 80/20 confounding and no true signal in simulation (more with more features), and it warns about this too. The default stays unprotected, the conservative choice. Under protect = TRUE, outcome effects are estimated from within-batch variation only, only batch locations are adjusted (per- batch scaling would rescale the protected outcome effect), and when every batch holds a single class only differences between batches of the same class are removed. A batch that cannot be separated from the outcome at all is left unadjusted, with a warning. fit_resample() reports each kind of batch/outcome diagnostic once across folds.

  • keep_batch_col = TRUE keeps the batch column intact. A kept batch column was batch-adjusted along with the features, which zeroed it out; it is now passed through unadjusted.

  • Batch scale is measured as in ComBat. Each batch’s scale is now taken relative to the pooled within-batch residual variance, not the grand variance that included between-batch differences. The old version over-inflated within-batch spread after adjustment whenever batches differed in location.

  • delta_lsi() inference replaced: corrected repeated-CV t-test. Repeated cross-validation re-uses the same data, so fold and repeat differences are correlated. The previous sign-flip tests treated them as independent and were badly anti-conservative with real model fits under a true null: 70% type-I error at alpha = 0.05 for 5-fold x 10 repeats on 100 samples, and 14-17% for the group-level test on leave-one-study-out designs. delta_lsi() now uses the Nadeau & Bengio (2003) corrected variance (1/J + n_test/n_train) * var(fold deltas) with a t reference on folds per repeat - 1 degrees of freedom (calibrated df, Bouckaert 2003), for every exchangeability setting. Folds that re-use an identical test set are counted once. In real-fit simulations (subject-grouped, batch-blocked, leave-one-study-out and rolling-origin designs, 1-20 repeats) type-I error stayed at or below 5%. CIs for delta_metric and delta_lsi use the same standard error; the BCa bootstrap is gone.

    • R_eff is now the number of folds per repeat (studies for study_loocv), not the number of repeats: repeats sharpen the estimate but add no independent units, so they no longer raise the tier.
    • Tiers: D below 3 folds per repeat or unpaired; C 3-9; B 10-19; A 20+. Tier labels are unchanged for compatibility; tiers A-C all report a p-value and CIs, and inference_ok is TRUE whenever they are finite.
    • exchangeability is stored and reported only. block_size, M_boot, M_flip and seed are ignored (a warning is issued for block_size).
    • info gains test, se, df, rho, n_fold_deltas, n_test_sets and folds_per_repeat; return_details = TRUE adds fold_deltas. min_p_achievable, block_size_used and n_blocks are now NA.

  • delta_lsi() pairs fits at the fold level. A fold whose metric is missing in either fit is dropped from both, so the paired difference always compares the same test sets; previously one all-NA repeat in one fit made the comparison unpaired, and an NA fold was dropped from one side only. The per-pipeline summaries (repeats_naive, repeats_guarded, info$metric_naive, info$metric_guarded) use the same paired folds.

  • delta_lsi() sizes compact-split folds correctly. Fold sizes come from fold_assignments, and training sizes are rebuilt the way fit_resample() builds them (past rows only for time_series, minus horizon / purge / embargo; secondary-constraint exclusions for combined). Compact plans previously weighted every fold equally and used “all non-test rows” as the training size, so the same plan could give different results in compact and explicit form.

  • delta_lsi() metric direction. Auto-detection now treats mape, smape, mase, *_cost, ece, fpr, nll, cross_entropy and other loss/error names as lower-is-better (several were read as higher-is-better, flipping the sign of the result), recognises skill scores and explained-deviance (e.g. brier_skill_score) and yardstick names such as kap, ccc and roc_aunp as higher-is-better, and warns when a metric name is not recognised instead of silently assuming higher is better.

  • cv_ci(method = "nadeau_bengio") uses calibrated degrees of freedom. Its t reference now uses folds_per_repeat - 1 degrees of freedom (new argument) instead of all folds - 1, and no longer switches to the normal distribution at 30 or more folds; counting repeats as independent made the intervals too narrow for repeated CV (the same issue fixed in delta_lsi()); in a real-fit simulation of 5-fold x 10 CV, coverage of the 95% interval rose from 0.92 to 0.98. fit_resample() and tune_resample() pass it. Invalid n_train, n_test or folds_per_repeat are now errors. Requesting "nadeau_bengio" without n_train / n_test now warns: the correction cannot be applied and the uncorrected variance is used.

  • cv_ci() defaults to method = "nadeau_bengio" and accepts a LeakFit. The previous default, "normal", treats folds as independent; in a real-fit simulation of repeated 5-fold CV its 95% interval covered the true expected performance only 37% of the time (vs 98% for the corrected method). Calls without a method now get the corrected interval. Passing the fit itself (cv_ci(fit)) supplies the fold sizes and folds per repeat; a bare metrics data frame without n_train / n_test warns. Use method = "normal" to get the old behaviour.

  • tune_resample() confidence intervals are corrected. It requested the Nadeau-Bengio correction without train/test sizes, so the uncorrected variance was used silently; it now passes the outer folds’ average sizes and folds per repeat.

  • Compact and explicit time-series plans train on the same row order. Compact plans rebuilt the training rows in row order instead of time order, so order-dependent learners (e.g. ranger with a fixed seed) gave different results for the same plan.

  • Grouped time series reports lost folds. In make_split_plan(mode = "time_series", group = ), a later time block whose training set comes out empty (every earlier row belongs to its own test groups, or horizon / purge / embargo leave nothing) was dropped silently. It now warns with the number of blocks lost, the reason, and how many rows are tested (e.g. 16 of 64 where 48 were expected); rolling-origin CV’s untested first block is not counted as a loss.

  • Grouped time series: the panel fallback says what it does. When every group appears across the time range, make_split_plan(mode = "time_series", group = ) uses a panel fallback that tests every group but trains only on rows before the earliest test time. It now warns with the training share it achieves (often about 20%) and suggests alternatives. (Staggered rolling-origin cutoffs were tried; they train on more history but leave rows, and on unbalanced panels whole groups, never tested.) When regular folds lose blocks, both plans are built and the one with the larger sum(test rows x training rows) is kept, so a fallback that tests more rows but trains on very few does not replace a well-trained regular plan; the warning names the plan kept and both plans’ coverage. Fallback folds now follow the same minimum of 3 test rows as regular folds; the warning gives the actual reasons blocks were lost, and when neither plan yields a fold the error says why.

  • fit_resample()’s “No successful folds were completed” error now gives the fold errors or the skip reason (e.g. every requested metric was NA on single-class test folds). The metric_summary docs now say that _mean / _sd summarize all fold rows while _ci_lo / _ci_hi count each distinct test set once.

Breaking changes

  • delta_lsi() tier labels renamed to describe the test they report: "A_full_inference" -> "A_ttest_ge20_folds", "B_signflip_ci" -> "B_ttest_10_19_folds", "C_signflip" -> "C_ttest_3_9_folds" ("D_insufficient" unchanged). The old names referred to the bootstrap and sign-flip inference that the corrected t-test replaced; code comparing dlsi_tier() or @tier with the old strings must be updated.

  • as_leaksplits() requires the data’s sample IDs to match the spec’s exactly. Missing, duplicated or extra IDs (in either direction) are an error; previously extra rows in data were dropped silently by the join.

New features

  • audit_leakage() with the default perm_refit = "auto" now says what a refit costs before running it (B x folds model fits) and says when it falls back to fixed-prediction permutations because B exceeds perm_refit_auto_max (previously silent). The fallback message no longer calls the fixed-prediction test “slightly liberal” (JSS review, K1).
  • audit_leakage() reports how many near-duplicate pairs are expected by chance and the ratio observed / expected (info$duplicate_null; JSS review, L3.4). The expected count applies the same rule to null rows drawn from a Gaussian copula with the features’ marginals and rank correlation; duplicate_null_reps (default 3, 0 skips) sets the number of draws. On data without duplicates (40 datasets each) the mean expected count was within about 25% of the mean observed count for Gaussian, skewed and discrete features. summary() prints both counts and, in the interpretation, lists the flagged leakage mechanisms; the flag rules of the mechanism summary are documented in ?audit_leakage (L3.5).
  • make_split_plan() gains stratify_method = c("groups", "rows") (JSS review, J8). The default "groups" keeps the current assignment (groups labelled by majority class, dealt round-robin), which balances numbers of groups, not rows. "rows" places groups largest first in the fold that keeps each class’s share of rows most even, as scikit-learn’s StratifiedGroupKFold does. In simulations with unequal group sizes and mixed-outcome groups (40 groups, 5 folds, 200 seeds), the largest deviation of a fold’s case share from the overall share averaged 0.022, against 0.134 for "groups" and 0.208 unstratified. Refit permutations, nested plans and tune_resample() inner splits re-use the recorded method.
  • as_leaksplits() covers more of the splitGraph contract. Specs with ordering_required = TRUE map to mode = "time_series" with group separation (train strictly earlier than test, no group in both); spec$stratum_var is forwarded as stratify_by; additional block columns (site_group, region_group, platform_group, assay_group) are carried; and use_block_constraints enforces chosen block_vars as secondary axes through make_split_plan(mode = "combined").
  • make_split_plan() gains stratify_by (stratify on a column other than the outcome), group-disjoint time_series splits (group = with time =) with a longitudinal panel fallback, and more axis types for mode = "combined" (site, region, platform, assay, relatedness, spatial).
  • guard_fit() gains train-only frozen normalisations (normalize$method = "quantile", "log_cpm", "clr") and train-only batch adjustment (steps$batch_adjust; see the bug fixes above for its behaviour).
  • Recipe checks flag recipes with already-trained steps and step_mutate() / step_filter() calls to global summaries (mean(), sd(), quantile(), …), which leak test-set statistics at bake().
  • fit_resample() and tune_resample() drop split metadata columns (sample ID, stratification and constraint columns) from the predictors.

bioLeak 0.3.8

CRAN release: 2026-05-21

Bug fixes (results can change)

  • AUC orientation. AUC was computed with pROC::roc(truth, pred) using pROC’s default direction = "auto", which silently flips the curve when predictions are anti-correlated with the outcome. A perfectly inverted model scored AUC = 1, AUC could never fall below about 0.5, and permutation nulls centred above 0.5 (0.51-0.57 observed). AUC is now always oriented, with explicit levels = c(negative, positive) and direction = "<" (the positive class is the second outcome level, as set by positive_class), through a single internal helper used by fit_resample() and audit_leakage() (observed metric and permutation null). The univariate and multivariate target scans already used an oriented rank AUC and now share the same helper. Anti-correlated predictions now give AUC < 0.5, and label-permutation nulls centre at 0.5. The target-scan flagging score = |AUC - 0.5| * 2 is unchanged, so strong inverse proxies are still flagged.

  • simulate_leakage_suite() prevalence. The outcome generator used pnorm(linpred - qnorm(prevalence)), which inverted the requested prevalence (0.2 gave about 0.72; 0.8 gave about 0.27). It now uses pnorm(linpred + b0) with b0 = qnorm(prevalence) * sqrt(1 + signal_strength^2), which also corrects the attenuation from the latent-variable scale, so the marginal prevalence equals the requested value at every signal_strength. The imaging_tabular (0.4) and ehr_tabular (0.3) profiles of benchmark_leakage_suite() now have their declared prevalence.

  • as_leaksplits() for all splitGraph modes. The splitGraph modes site, region, platform, assay, relatedness and spatial failed with “subscript out of bounds” (the subject_grouped fallback was unreachable), and composite failed with “‘primary_axis’ must be a list”. These modes, including both composite strategies, now map to make_split_plan(mode = "subject_grouped", group = "group_id"), which keeps each splitGraph dependency group intact within a fold. Composite specs that require ordering, specs whose constraint collapses all samples into one group, and column-name clashes between data and the spec give clear errors; unrecognised future modes fall back to grouped folds with a warning. bioLeak now has its own as_leaksplits() tests.

  • Batch-confounding rule corrected for multiplicity. The confounding_alignment rule of the audit mechanism summary took the raw minimum chi-square p-value over all batch columns and CV repeats, so a chance p = 0.038 in one of 10 repeats flagged an unrelated batch. audit_leakage() now adds a Holm-adjusted pval_adj column to batch_assoc (family = all batch-column x repeat rows), and the rule flags only when a row has pval_adj <= 0.05 and Cramer’s V >= 0.1. With a single repeat and one batch column the rule is unchanged.

  • Guarded variance/IQR filter uses the original scale. guard_fit() applied filter$var_thresh / filter$iqr_thresh after z-scoring, where every non-constant feature has variance 1, making var_thresh meaningless under the default normalize = "zscore" (and distorted under "robust"). The thresholds, and the min_keep ranking, now use the variance and IQR of the imputed training data before normalization. The pipeline order and the default (var_thresh = 0, iqr_thresh = 0, no filtering) are unchanged.

  • Refit permutation null for stratified plans (results can change). audit_leakage(perm_refit = TRUE) refitted on permuted outcomes but kept the observed folds, which make_split_plan(stratify = TRUE) had balanced on the true labels. Under permuted labels, and especially under group-restricted permutations, the fold class balance then varied widely. Each fold model’s baseline tracks its training balance, which is anti-correlated with its test balance, so pooled AUC under the null was biased below 0.5. This is the stratification bias of Parker, Günter and Bedo (2007, BMC Bioinformatics 8:326). The result was an inflated gap and an anti-conservative p-value. In a pure-noise grouped design (40 families of six plus 24 singletons), the fixed-fold null centred at 0.40-0.46, with about two-thirds of draws below 0.5. On one simulated design, using re-drawn folds and fold-mean AUC cut the gap from 0.235 to 0.158 and raised p from 0.0099 to 0.050. New argument perm_folds = c("auto", "fixed", "redraw"): "redraw" re-draws the split plan for each permutation with make_split_plan() on the permuted outcome. It uses the same mode, grouping columns, constraints, v, repeats and stratify, with seed splits@info$seed + b. The default, "auto", re-draws whenever the plan is stratified and can be rebuilt. Unstratified plans keep their observed folds, so their results are unchanged.

  • Unrestricted refit nulls are no longer silent. When the refit metadata lacks the outcome or the design column, the refit null is an unrestricted label shuffle that ignores the grouping. The common trigger is perm_refit_spec$x without the group column and no perm_refit_spec$coldata, which includes the refit data that fit_resample() stores by default. audit_leakage() now raises a bioLeak_permutation_warning in that case, naming the missing column. No warning is raised when the grouping has one sample per group (for example group = "row_id").

Behaviour changes and new arguments

  • audit_leakage() gains perm_summary = c("pooled", "fold_mean"). "fold_mean" scores the observed fit and each permutation by the mean of per-fold metric values instead of the metric on predictions pooled across folds. Between-fold baseline shifts cannot bias it, and Parker et al.

    1. recommend it for AUC. Refit audits report both summaries in audit_info(aud)$perm_gap_summaries. The default, "pooled", keeps the previous behaviour.

  • audit_info(aud) now records the null used: perm_null is "global_shuffle", "refit_fixed_folds" or "refit_redrawn_folds" (previously "refit" for every refit null). It also records perm_folds, perm_folds_reason, perm_scheme ("group_restricted", "within_batch", "within_study", "time_block", "unrestricted" or "global_shuffle"), perm_summary and perm_gap_summaries. summary() prints the fold handling, the permutation scheme and the summary statistic for refit nulls.

  • audit_leakage() with perm_refit = FALSE: the permutation-gap null is, by design, a global label shuffle of the pooled out-of-fold predictions. A restricted permutation source was also built on this path but never used, so perm_stratify, time_block and block_len silently had no effect. The dead code is removed, a warning is now raised when any of these is set on the fixed-prediction path, the documentation says which null each argument affects, and info$perm_null records the null used (see the entry above for its values).

  • fit_resample() gains id_cols, a character vector of identifier or metadata columns to exclude from the predictors (previously only the outcome and the split’s group/batch/study/time columns were dropped, so a character sample_id was one-hot encoded into one predictor per row). With guarded preprocessing, a bioLeak_input_warning is raised when a character or factor column not listed in id_cols has at least 90% unique values. id_cols is stored in the fit and reused by refit-based permutations in audit_leakage().

Documentation

  • delta_lsi(): the exact two-sided sign-flip test has minimum achievable p-value 2 / 2^R_eff, so tier C_signflip at R_eff = 5 can never reach p < 0.05 (minimum 0.0625); 6 or more paired repeats are needed. The tier documentation and vignette (which gave 1 / 2^R) are corrected, the floor is stored in info$min_p_achievable (using n_blocks for exchangeability = "blocked_time"), and summary() notes when it exceeds 0.05. Tier boundaries are unchanged.

bioLeak 0.3.7

CRAN release: 2026-04-29

Documentation

  • The vignette previously mixed defensive requireNamespace() checks with bare library(<suggests_pkg>) calls; the bare calls would hard-error if the suggested package was not installed, defeating the defensive checks elsewhere in the same vignette. The tidymodels-interop chunk now carries eval = requireNamespace("recipes", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("yardstick", quietly = TRUE) in its chunk header, so the chunk is skipped (rather than erroring) during vignette build when those Suggests packages are absent. The parallel-setup chunk gains a brief comment documenting that future is a Suggests dependency. A regression test (test-vignette-suggests.R) walks the vignette and asserts that every chunk-level library(<suggests_pkg>) call is inside an appropriately gated chunk.

API improvements (no behavior change)

  • predict_guard() is now also accessible through the standard [stats::predict()] generic via a registered S3 method predict.GuardFit(). Calling predict(fit, newdata) on a GuardFit object dispatches to predict.GuardFit() and yields output that is bit-identical to the legacy predict_guard(fit, newdata). predict_guard() is preserved as a thin backward-compatible alias, so existing code continues to work without modification. methods(class = "GuardFit") now returns print, summary, and predict, restoring the standard R idiom for transformer objects.

  • Added show() / print() methods to the public result classes that previously only had summary():

    • LeakFit: new show() (S4) — brief auto-print giving task, outcome, learners, fold count, and fold-status one-liner.
    • LeakAudit: new show() (S4) — brief auto-print giving task, outcome, permutation-gap statistics, and component row counts (batch association, target leakage, duplicates).
    • LeakTune: new print() (S3) — brief auto-print giving outer-fold success rate, tuning-grid size, selection rule, and refit status. Each method ends with a one-line hint pointing to summary(<obj>) for the full diagnostic report. methods(class = ...) now returns show/print alongside summary for all three classes.

Renames (no behavior change)

  • .guard_fit() is renamed to guard_fit() and .guard_ensure_levels() is renamed to guard_ensure_levels(). Leading-dot prefixes on exported functions are unconventional and were causing the renamed helpers to appear awkwardly in help(package = "bioLeak"). Behavior, arguments, and return values are unchanged; only the names move from the dot-prefixed form to ordinary names. Internal callers (fit_resample(), impute_guarded(), predict_guard()’s documentation, and the package vignette) are updated to use the new names.

New features

  • Added public accessor functions for the S4 result classes so that downstream code (replication scripts, vignettes, and end-user analyses) can read components of LeakFit, LeakAudit, and LeakDeltaLSI objects without reaching into S4 internals via @. The new accessors are purely additive; slot definitions are unchanged and existing code that uses @ continues to work.
    • LeakFit: fit_metrics().
    • LeakAudit: audit_perm_gap(), audit_batch_assoc(), audit_target_assoc(), audit_duplicates(), audit_info().
    • LeakDeltaLSI: dlsi_metric(), dlsi_robust(), dlsi_ci(), dlsi_p_value(), dlsi_tier(), dlsi_R_eff(), dlsi_repeats(). Each accessor performs an is(x, "<Class>") validation and emits an informative error when called on the wrong object.

bioLeak 0.3.5

CRAN release: 2026-03-26

Breaking changes

  • delta_lsi(): inference tier strings renamed to accurately reflect what each tier provides. "C_point_only" → "C_signflip" (the sign-flip p-value is available at this tier, not just point estimates); "B_ci_only" → "B_signflip_ci" (both the sign-flip p-value and BCa CI are available). Code that compares result@tier against the old string literals must be updated.

New features

  • delta_lsi() gains a block_size argument and makes exchangeability actionable for "blocked_time" inputs. When exchangeability = "blocked_time", the sign-flip test now uses a block procedure that flips contiguous blocks of repeats together, preserving serial autocorrelation under the null. block_size is auto-estimated from the AR(1) of the repeat-level deltas when NULL (default) and capped at floor(R/3) to guarantee at least three independent blocks. The @info slot gains block_size_used and n_blocks fields. If the block structure yields fewer than five independent blocks, @p_value is set to NA and a warning is issued.
  • delta_lsi() now emits an explicit warning when exchangeability is "by_group" or "within_batch", informing users that those modes are stored but inference still uses the iid sign-flip procedure. Previously these values were accepted silently without affecting computation.

Bug fixes and improvements

  • fit_resample(): compact + combined mode now correctly excludes constraint-axis violations from training sets. Previously the compact fallback used setdiff(all, test), ignoring multi-axis constraints declared via make_split_plan(constraints = ...). The same fix is applied in the as_rsample() conversion path for consistency.
  • Guarded preprocessing: lasso and t-test feature selection now uses name-based column selection in the transform step, preventing index misalignment when constant columns are removed during fitting.
  • delta_lsi(): R_eff and the inference tier are now recomputed after repeat-level intersection, so that dropped all-NA repeats correctly reduce the effective sample size and select the appropriate tier.
  • fit_resample(): fold error messages are now correctly captured when running in parallel via future.apply. Previously <<- mutations inside worker processes were silently lost; errors are now attached as result attributes and extracted after the parallel map.
  • tune_resample(): fold-ID columns (id, id2, .notes) no longer leak into hyperparameter aggregation in the internal select_config() helper.
  • summary.LeakFit() now returns object@metric_summary invisibly, matching the documented return value (previously returned the object itself).
  • Fixed vignette (bioLeak-intro) referencing a shadowed data frame for sample count; now reads from fit_safe@splits@info$coldata.
  • Fixed audit_leakage() roxygen documenting a duplicates column named in_train_test; the actual column name is cross_fold.
  • make_split_plan(): time-series mode now warns and skips folds with fewer than 3 test samples instead of producing degenerate folds.
  • fit_resample(): added bounds checking for repeat_id in compact fold resolution to produce a clear error instead of a cryptic index failure.
  • show() and summary() for LeakDeltaLSI now label the sign-flip p-value as testing mean(Δr) (delta_metric), not delta_lsi, making the estimator–inference pairing explicit.
  • summary() prints a diagnostic note when the sign-flip p-value and BCa CI lead to qualitatively different conclusions (one significant, one spanning zero), which can occur when outlier repeats pull the arithmetic mean away from the Huber estimate.
  • summary() prints the block size and number of blocks used when exchangeability = "blocked_time".

bioLeak 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-03-05

New features

  • Added N-axis combined splitting via constraints in make_split_plan(), generalizing beyond two-axis combined CV while preserving train/test exclusion across all declared axes.
  • Added compact = TRUE split storage (fold assignments) for large datasets to reduce split object memory footprint.
  • Added check_split_overlap() for explicit overlap-invariant validation across fold/group axes.
  • Added cv_ci() (with Nadeau-Bengio correction) and integrated CI columns into fit_resample() and tune_resample() metric summaries (*_ci_lo, *_ci_hi).
  • Added guard_to_recipe() to map guarded preprocessing configurations to recipes pipelines with explicit fallback/warning behavior.
  • Added benchmark_leakage_suite() for reproducible modality-by-mechanism benchmark grids and detection-rate summaries.
  • Expanded audit_leakage() diagnostics with mechanism taxonomy fields (mechanism_class, taxonomy, mechanism_summary) and richer risk attribution outputs.
  • Added FDR-aware target scan outputs (p_value_adj, flag_fdr) with selectable multiple-testing correction (target_p_adjust, target_alpha).
  • Added feature_space (raw/rank) and duplicate_scope (train_test/all) controls for duplicate diagnostics.
  • Strengthened permutation auditing with explicit perm_mode handling for rsample-derived splits and safer perm_refit = "auto" behavior.
  • Extended tidymodels interoperability: rsample conversion and metadata inference are more robust (split_cols = "auto", mode/perm-mode propagation, stricter compatibility checks).
  • Improved nested tuning safety in tune_resample(): final refit now aggregates hyperparameters across outer folds (median/majority) instead of selecting a single best outer fold.
  • Added binomial threshold tuning support in tune_resample() using inner-fold predictions (tune_threshold, threshold_grid, threshold_metric).
  • Added structured fold-status tracking (fold_status) and elapsed timing in both fitting and tuning paths for better failure-mode observability.
  • Added strict-mode and validation-policy infrastructure (bioLeak.strict, bioLeak.validation_mode) with structured condition classes for safer recipe and workflow guardrails.
  • Added provenance capture (.bio_capture_provenance) and attached provenance metadata to LeakFit, LeakAudit, and LeakTune.
  • Improved summary.LeakAudit() output with explicit Mechanism Risk Assessment reporting.
  • Hardened recipe preprocessing in fit_resample() to avoid fold-time failures when recipes reference split metadata columns (for example subject).
  • Updated simulation defaults and audit settings for more practical runtime (simulate_leakage_suite() default B, auto refit cap handling).
  • Updated manuscript/simulation assets under paper/ with refreshed large-scale simulation outputs and case-study artifacts.

bioLeak 0.2.0

CRAN release: 2026-02-11

New features

  • Leak-safe hyperparameter tuning via tune_resample(): nested cross-validation using tidymodels tune/dials with leakage-aware outer splits.
  • Tidymodels interoperability: fit_resample() now accepts rsample rset/rsplit objects as splits, recipes::recipe for preprocessing, workflows::workflow as learner, and yardstick::metric_set for metrics. as_rsample() converts LeakSplits to an rsample rset.
  • Parsnip model specs accepted directly as the learner argument in fit_resample().
  • Diagnostics polish: new calibration_summary() and plot_calibration() for probability calibration checks; confounder_sensitivity() and plot_confounder_sensitivity() for sensitivity analysis.
  • Simulation utility simulate_leakage_suite() for generating controlled leakage scenarios and benchmarking audit sensitivity.
  • HTML audit report via audit_report(): renders a self-contained HTML summary of all audit results for sharing and review.
  • Multi-learner auditing with audit_leakage_by_learner() to audit each learner in a multi-model fit separately.
  • Multivariate target leakage scan enabled by default in audit_leakage() for supported tasks, complementing the existing univariate scan.
  • Refit-based permutations (perm_refit = TRUE or "auto") in audit_leakage() for a more powerful permutation gap test when refit data are available.
  • Class weights support in fit_resample() for imbalanced classification tasks.
  • New plotting functions: plot_fold_balance(), plot_overlap_checks(), plot_perm_distribution(), plot_time_acf().

Improvements

  • S4 classes (LeakSplits, LeakFit, LeakAudit) now include setValidity checks for slot consistency.
  • summary() methods for LeakFit, LeakAudit, and LeakTune improved with clearer console output and edge-case handling.
  • impute_guarded() gains enhanced diagnostics and RNG safety.
  • .guard_fit() and .guard_ensure_levels() made more robust with better error messages.
  • Permutation label factory (permute_labels) gains verbose mode, digest-based caching, and improved stratification safety.
  • audit_leakage() handles NA metrics gracefully and enriches trail metadata.
  • make_split_plan() improved stratification logic and reproducible seeding.
  • audit_report() now renders from a temporary copy of the Rmd template to avoid write failures on read-only file systems (e.g. during R CMD check).
  • Comprehensive vignette (bioLeak-intro) rewritten with guided workflow and leaky-vs-correct comparisons.

Bug fixes

  • Fixed fit_resample() result aggregation when folds fail during preprocessing.
  • Fixed missForest preprocessing dropping rows.
  • Fixed single-level factors causing errors in guarded preprocessing.
  • Fixed filter keep-column alignment by name.
  • Fixed glmnet folds receiving non-numeric design matrices.
  • Fixed constant imputation for categorical data.
  • Fixed RANN self-neighbour filter in duplicate detection.
  • Fixed various edge cases in outcome extraction and hashing utilities.
  • Resolved multiple CRAN check issues (Rd formatting, example runtime, read-only file-system writes).

bioLeak 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-02-06

  • Initial release.
  • Core pipeline: make_split_plan() for leakage-aware splitting (subject-grouped, batch-blocked, study leave-out, time-ordered); fit_resample() for cross-validated fitting with built-in guarded preprocessing (train-only imputation, normalisation, filtering, feature selection).
  • Leakage auditing: audit_leakage() with label-permutation gap test, batch/study association tests, univariate target leakage scan, and near-duplicate detection.
  • Guarded preprocessing helpers: impute_guarded(), predict_guard(), .guard_fit(), .guard_ensure_levels().
  • S4 class system: LeakSplits, LeakFit, LeakAudit.
  • Support for binomial, multiclass, regression, and survival tasks.
  • Built-in learners: glm, glmnet, ranger, xgboost (via custom_learners).
  • SummarizedExperiment input support.
  • Vignette and comprehensive documentation.
